getting-started.name: Getting started tour
getting-started.description: A quick guided tour of the core dashboard areas.

steps.title: Welcome to Northstar
steps.body: This quick tour shows the key areas of the dashboard and where to find help at any time.

steps.title: Track your KPIs
steps.body: These cards summarize what matters most. They’re a common place to attach contextual guidance when users are learning.

steps.title: Filters & saved views
steps.body: Power users can save filter presets. Walkthrough steps can be anchored to controls like this and explain impact before a user changes anything.

steps.title: Contextual help is one click away
steps.body: Look for the (?) icon across the UI. It opens contextual help with ‘Show me how’ to start a guided walkthrough.

saved-views.name: Saved views walkthrough
saved-views.description: Show how to create and reuse a saved view.

steps.title: Start with filters
steps.body: Choose filters to narrow your dataset. We’ll save this as a reusable view.

steps.title: Save the current view
steps.body: Click here to save your current filters as a named view. In a real app, this might open a modal.

steps.title: Switch between views
steps.body: Saved views can be shared with teammates and used to standardize reporting.

missing-target-demo.name: Missing target demo
missing-target-demo.description: Demonstrates graceful handling when a selector is not found.

steps.title: Graceful fallback when targets change
steps.body: If the UI changes or a feature is gated, the DAP shouldn’t break. This step intentionally points to a missing element.

assist-mode.name: Assist Mode walkthrough
assist-mode.description: Shows how Assist Mode helps users fill a form when they’re unsure.

steps.title: Turn on Assist Mode
steps.body: Assist Mode can proactively guide users when they hesitate, hit validation errors, or ask for help.

steps.title: Contextual guidance per field
steps.body: Click into a field and pause for a moment. The assistant will suggest what to enter, with an example you can apply.

steps.title: Help on validation errors
steps.body: If a user enters an invalid email, Assist Mode can explain what’s expected and offer a valid example.

customers-tour.name: Customers walkthrough
customers-tour.description: Shows how to use the customers table and the detail drawer.

steps.title: Find customers quickly
steps.body: Search and filters help teams narrow down accounts before taking action.

steps.title: Import customers
steps.body: DAP can explain what data is required and what happens after import.

steps.title: Scan the customer table
steps.body: Tables are common DAP surfaces: tooltips on headers, guidance on columns, and “next best action” nudges.

steps.title: Open the customer drawer
steps.body: Click a row to see details. DAP can guide users inside nested UI like drawers or modals.

campaigns-tour.name: Campaigns walkthrough
campaigns-tour.description: Shows how to create and schedule a campaign.

steps.title: Create a campaign
steps.body: Empty states are a great place to guide new users toward the primary action.

steps.title: Choose a template
steps.body: Templates reduce cognitive load. DAP can recommend which template fits a goal.

steps.title: Schedule safely
steps.body: Explain what timing means (timezone, send window, and expected impact).

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: Confirm what happens next. DAP can reduce mistakes by summarizing before launch.

filters-help.title: Filters
filters-help.summary: Filters narrow your results and can be saved as reusable views.
readMore: Use filters to focus on a segment (e.g., enterprise customers, a region, or a time range).
Saved views help teams standardize reporting and reduce repetitive setup.

kpis-help.title: KPI cards
kpis-help.summary: These KPIs update in real time as filters change.
readMore: KPI cards are great for quick health checks and daily monitoring.
In production, a DAP might include guidance on interpreting metrics and recommended actions.

customers-import-help.title: Import customers
customers-import-help.summary: Upload a CSV to create or update accounts in bulk.
readMore: Recommended columns: company name, domain, plan, seat count, and a primary contact email.
In production, you’d validate rows and show a preview before applying changes.

customers-health-help.title: Health
customers-health-help.summary: A quick signal of adoption risk based on usage trends and key events.
readMore: Healthy: steady usage and recent key actions.
Watch: declining usage or incomplete onboarding.
At risk: sharp drop or critical workflow failures.

campaigns-templates-help.title: Templates
campaigns-templates-help.summary: Templates speed up campaign creation and reduce setup errors.
readMore: Choose a template aligned to your goal (activation, adoption, or renewal).
In a real app, templates would come with recommended audiences and messaging.

campaigns-schedule-help.title: Scheduling
campaigns-schedule-help.summary: Pick when a campaign starts (timezone-aware) and who should receive it.
readMore: Avoid scheduling during peak usage if the campaign is disruptive.
For rollouts, consider a staged approach by segment.

companyName.label: Company name
companyName.hint: Use the legal company name or the name your team recognizes internally.

website.label: Website
website.hint: A public URL helps us enrich account details. Use the root domain.

industry.label: Industry
industry.hint: Choose the closest match. This is used only for benchmarking and reporting.

teamSize.label: Team size
teamSize.hint: Enter the approximate number of active seats for this account.

billingEmail.label: Billing email
billingEmail.hint: Use an address that receives invoices and renewal notices.
readMore: Avoid personal emails when possible (e.g., firstname@…).
If billing is handled by finance, use a shared inbox.

goal.label: Primary goal
goal.hint: What outcome does the customer want? This helps tailor onboarding guidance.
goal.example: Improve onboarding completion for new admins
